courseTitle: Thinking like an attacker: threat models and security principles
lessonTitle: Attack trees: start from the attacker's goal
md: The numbers are estimates and the tree is never complete. Schneier calls the safe example incomplete and warns not to read its values as a statement about how secure a real safe is. Use trees to compare options and find the cheapest path, not to claim an attack costs exactly 2,200.

courseTitle: Tiered memory: placing pages across DRAM, CXL and SSD
lessonTitle: How Linux ranks nodes into tiers: abstract distance
md: Tiers are not the same as NUMA distance. A remote-socket DRAM node is far, but it has CPUs and DRAM-class performance, so it sits in the top tier and is never a demotion target for the other socket. Only slower memory types form lower tiers.

courseTitle: Time-series forecasting: baselines, smoothing and honest backtests
lessonTitle: Prophet, the M4 competition and foundation models
md: Misconception: a bigger or newer model will beat simple methods. On the M4 data pure ML lost to simple combinations, and on our toy series SES with a fitted alpha was no better than naive. Any model, from Prophet to a foundation model, has to beat seasonal naive under rolling-origin evaluation before it ships.

courseTitle: TLS and PKI in practice
lessonTitle: Revocation: CRL, OCSP, stapling, and why short-lived certs won
md: "We revoked the certificate, so we are safe" is wishful thinking. Revocation reaches clients slowly and unreliably. Assume a compromised certificate is usable until it expires, and size your lifetimes accordingly.

courseTitle: Triton kernels: block-level GPU programming
lessonTitle: Autotuning, num_warps, num_stages and when to use Triton
md: Autotuning has costs you do not see in steady state: the first call for each new `key` value compiles and benchmarks every config, and each distinct constexpr combination is a separate compiled kernel. Keep `key` to arguments that really change the best config, and use `prune_configs_by` to drop hopeless candidates.

courseTitle: Unified multimodal models: one transformer that reads and draws
lessonTitle: Evaluating unified models and choosing a design
md: No axis is free. Discrete plus causal is the simplest to train and serve; continuous plus bidirectional plus separate encoders has led the reported GenEval numbers in these papers, at the cost of more moving parts. Pick based on what the product must do well, then evaluate both sides of the model.

courseTitle: Unikernels: one application, one address space, one VM image
lessonTitle: Booting on the hypervisor: virtual devices, boot time and memory
md: Do not assume every unikernel does this. Sealing and compile-time randomization are Mirage's design; a 2019 study by the security firm NCC Group of two other unikernels, Rumprun and IncludeOS, found ASLR, W xor X and stack canaries (a random value placed before a function's return address and checked on return, so a buffer overflow is caught) absent or broken.

courseTitle: Vector database internals: SIMD kernels, segments and disk
lessonTitle: Graph traversal: memory layout, cache misses and prefetching
md: In graph search the expensive part per hop is often the first touch of a random vector, not the arithmetic. Contiguous fixed-size blocks, aligned vectors, prefetching and smaller (compressed) vectors all attack that same miss.

courseTitle: verl: the HybridFlow RL training stack for LLMs
lessonTitle: One GRPO step through the V1 trainer, call by call
md: Read the source, not just the prose. verl's GSM8K example page says the scorer gives 0.1 for a well-formatted wrong answer, but in the current `gsm8k.py` the default `format_score` is 0.0 (the quickstart page also says 0.0). A silent difference like that changes what the policy is rewarded for.

courseTitle: Video-LLMs with long-video memory
lessonTitle: Bigger context or captions: LongVA, Gemini 1.5, retrieval, benchmarks
md: Choose by the question. Sparse sampling plus pooling suits gist questions. Merging and memory banks suit streaming and bounded memory. Long context gives the most faithful view at the highest cost. Caption retrieval is cheapest per question and reuses work across questions, but only knows what the captioner wrote.

courseTitle: Virtualization and hypervisor security
lessonTitle: I/O virtualization: emulation, virtio, passthrough and the IOMMU
md: EPT/NPT confines what the guest's *CPU* can touch; the IOMMU confines what the guest's *devices* can touch. Device assignment without an IOMMU (or with a group shared across tenants) quietly removes the memory wall from lesson 3.

courseTitle: Virtualization and hypervisor security
lessonTitle: Confidential VMs: SEV-SNP, TDX and Arm CCA stop trusting the host
md: A confidential VM moves trust from the host's software to the CPU vendor's hardware and firmware. It protects memory and registers from a curious or compromised host, not availability, not the guest's own bugs, and not data the guest sends through shared pages unencrypted.

courseTitle: Fine-tuning a vision model (ViT)
lessonTitle: Linear probe, LoRA or full fine-tune: choosing what to train
md: Decide by data and shift. Little data or a frozen-feature baseline needed: linear probe. Many tasks on one backbone or tight memory: LoRA (adapters are tiny and merge for free). Plenty of data from the deployment distribution: full fine-tune. Expect distribution shift at deployment: probe first, then fine-tune (LP-FT).

courseTitle: Visual tokenizers: turning images into discrete tokens
lessonTitle: Vector quantization: snap each vector to its nearest code
md: A common misreading is that the straight-through estimator makes quantization differentiable. It does not: it substitutes the identity gradient. The encoder is updated as if the decoder had received $z_e$, which is a useful but biased approximation that is better when $z_e$ stays close to its code.

courseTitle: vLLM attention backends: selection, batching, KV layout, CUDA graphs
lessonTitle: Mixed prefill and decode in one forward pass
md: A mixed batch is one flat list of tokens plus offsets, sorted decodes first by the runner. Backends with one variable-length kernel do not care about the order. Backends with separate decode and prefill kernels split it with one index.

courseTitle: vLLM attention backends: selection, batching, KV layout, CUDA graphs
lessonTitle: CUDA graphs: padding, support levels and mode downgrades
md: Graph capture assumes `forward` does the same thing at replay as at capture. That is why `AttentionImpl.forward` must not branch on Python values that change per batch inside a full graph, and why builders write into persistent buffers instead of allocating new tensors.

courseTitle: Vision-language models for reading images
lessonTitle: Reading a receipt into validated JSON
md: Do not ask the model to fill in a missing total by computing it. Then the arithmetic check compares the model with itself and can never fail.

courseTitle: Wait-free algorithms: bounded progress for every thread
lessonTitle: A practical wait-free queue: phases and helping (Kogan-Petrank)
md: Two checks in `help_enq` look redundant but are not. The paper shows that replacing `while (isStillPending(tid, phase))` with `while (true)` breaks wait-freedom, and dropping the second `isStillPending` check just before the CAS on `last.next` breaks linearizability, because a thread that was suspended there could insert a node another helper already inserted.

courseTitle: Weather and climate foundation models: GraphCast to Aurora
lessonTitle: Foundation models, hybrids, and where these models break
md: "Foundation model" here does not mean a chatbot for weather. It means one pretrained network whose weights are reused and fine-tuned across forecasting tasks.

courseTitle: Web application testing and bug bounty practice
lessonTitle: Testing authorization at scale: two accounts and a replay matrix
md: If a replay ever returns another person's real data, stop. Do not page through more records to measure the scale. The disclose.io terms ask researchers to limit data access to the minimum needed for a proof of concept and to cease testing and report immediately when they encounter user data.

courseTitle: The browser security model
lessonTitle: How a page loads: HTML, subresources, JavaScript and the DOM
md: A script runs with the authority of **the page that includes it**, not the server it came from. `lib.js` from `cdn.example.net` runs as if `shop.example.com` had written it: it can read and change the shop's DOM, read the shop's visible cookies and send requests to the shop with the user's cookies. Including a script is handing over your keys.

courseTitle: The browser security model
lessonTitle: Subresource Integrity and the trust you hand to third-party scripts
md: SRI only works for files that never change between requests. It cannot pin a script that is generated per request or a library loaded as "latest". Pin exact versions, self-host what you can, and keep the list of third-party scripts on sensitive pages (login, payment) as short as possible.

courseTitle: Windows for security: accounts, processes, registry and event logs
lessonTitle: Event IDs that tell an intrusion story: 4688, 4720, 7045, 1102
md: Turn on command-line logging for 4688 (or deploy Sysmon). Without it you know rundll32.exe ran, but not what it was told to do, and that is usually the part that matters.

courseTitle: Wireless and mobile security
lessonTitle: Rogue access points, evil twins and how enterprises find them
md: An evil twin of an *open* network is indistinguishable from the real one at the Wi-Fi layer: there is nothing to authenticate. Users on open or OWE networks must rely on TLS (lesson 9) for everything that matters.

courseTitle: Wireless and mobile security
lessonTitle: Lockdown Mode, stalkerware and tracker abuse
md: For someone being monitored by an abuser, every defensive step can also alert the abuser: monitoring stopping, a tracker going silent. Technical help here should follow the person's own safety plan, ideally with a domestic violence support service, not just maximise security.

courseTitle: WSD learning-rate schedules
lessonTitle: Run it yourself: one stable trunk, three cooldown branches
md: Branch checklist: weights, optimizer state (including its step count), the global step that drives the LR schedule, and the data position. A loss spike on the first step of a branch means the optimizer state was not restored; a branch that starts with a warmup means the step counter was reset.

courseTitle: Zero-copy I/O: sendfile, splice and MSG_ZEROCOPY
lessonTitle: MSG_ZEROCOPY: sending from your own memory safely
md: A notification means "the kernel has released your pages", **not** "the data was delivered". With a deferred copy it can arrive before the copied data is even transmitted. Never use it as a transmit or delivery acknowledgement.

courseTitle: Zero-shot classification: labels chosen at inference time
lessonTitle: Evaluating zero-shot classifiers and choosing thresholds
md: The perfect F1 at 0.6 comes from 12 decisions on 3 hand-picked texts. A threshold tuned on so few examples is overfit. Use hundreds of labeled examples, and keep a separate test split to report the final number.
